How it works

Look. Approve. Done.

Three steps, all with your eyes. No hands, no voice, no special hardware.

  1. Look

    Point with your eyes. Hold your look on a button and it fills, then selects. A blink or a quick glance away doesn't break the hold.

  2. Approve

    Gemini plans the task and carries it out. Before it pays, sends, signs or calls, it shows you exactly what will happen and waits for your look.

  3. Done, and proven

    AGENCY checks every step by reading the screen back, then tells you plainly what happened, or what went wrong and what it will try next.

Next: Features

Features

Everything a day needs, a few looks away.

Each feature says where it really stands, as of 11 October 2026. “Works today” means it runs and is tested in the AGENCY app in our repository today.

Works today

A Gemini agent that asks first

Say what you want with a few looks. Gemini plans it in 1 to 8 steps and does them in Chrome and your apps, through a Chrome bridge, macOS accessibility, and computer use only as a last resort. It proves each step by reading the screen back.

  • Pay, send, sign, call, delete and share wait for your OK of that exact action. If anything changes, it asks again.
  • Spending limits: $50 a purchase, $100 a day by default.
  • It never handles passwords, two-factor codes or card numbers.

Uses practice (sandbox) stores by default. Real services only after someone sets them up.

Works today

Eye control with just a webcam

Eye scan · 5 seconds
  • Eye cursorThe default. Instant, no setup.
  • Eye gazeA 5-second eye scan: a light glides, then three check dots.

MediaPipe finds your eyes on the device and RealEye's open-source eye-image model reads where you look. The cursor glides smoothly, a held button survives a blink or a glance, and when two buttons are close, the AI's guess of your likely next one breaks the tie. Never for pay, send or sign.

Works today

Cloud AI that reads the network

  1. Sifter, on device, picks expert lenses
  2. Cisco sentinel measures the network
  3. Gemini thinks as hard as it allows
  • Ultra-FusionGood network. Gemini with full thinking.
  • Lean-FusionCongested. Gemini with light thinking.
  • Critical-FusionCritical. Built-in plans, at once.
  • Safe-ModeOffline. Built-in plans; Lifeline retries when back.

Every AI request goes through Ray's Synapse-Mesh first, so a bad signal slows the thinking down instead of leaving you stuck.

When Synapse-Mesh isn't running, AGENCY's built-in stand-in router chooses the mode.

Works today

Lifeline: help, one look away

  1. Three long blinks or a look at Help
  2. 8 seconds to cancel
  3. Your people, one after another, until someone says “I'm on my way”

It never calls 911 by itself. The people who come can.

Contacts are simulated phones until someone sets up real ones.

Works today

Talk, out loud

Build a sentence from big word and phrase boards and AGENCY says it out loud, in Apple's Personal Voice if you've made one. Listen mode shows what people say in big text, with replies one look away.

Works today

A calm Home that knows your usuals

Twelve big apps, from Talk and Food to Papers and Lifeline. AGENCY learns what you usually choose, like Friday's pad thai, and offers it first with a plain reason: “You chose this 4 of the last 5 Fridays”.

You can see, change or erase everything it remembers, and it stays on your computer.

Next: Safety and privacy

Safety and privacy

You stay in control. Always.

  • Your camera stays on your computer

    Video is processed on the device and thrown away. It's never stored and never sent. The cloud gets the task, never your face.

  • Nothing important without you

    Pay, send, sign, call, delete and share wait for your approval of that exact action. Change anything and it asks again. Stop works from every screen.

  • Spending limits

    $50 a purchase and $100 a day by default, on top of your approval.

  • Practice first

    Out of the box, stores are sandboxes and phones are simulated. Nobody real is contacted and nothing is bought until someone sets up the real thing.

  • No passwords in the AI's hands

    AGENCY never types, reads or keeps passwords, two-factor codes or card numbers.

  • Pages can't give orders

    Text on web pages, emails and documents is information, never instructions. If a page tries to steer the agent, it stops and shows you.

  • Not a medical device

    AGENCY isn't a medical device or a ventilator alarm and hasn't been clinically tested. Keep your existing alarms and care routines.

  • Not an emergency service

    Lifeline contacts the people you choose until one says they're coming. It never calls 911 by itself.

Read the full privacy policy, and how Lifeline is designed and what has and hasn't been tested in LIFELINE.md.

Next: Who it's for

Who it's for

People who can move their eyes, and the people around them.

AGENCY is for people living with ALS, locked-in syndrome, a high spinal cord injury, or anything else that takes away hands and voice but leaves the eyes.

Every part of it is judged by one question: is this safe and usable for someone who can't move or speak, and can't quickly undo a mistake?

For caregivers and family

  • You can set everything up with a mouse and keyboard; the person carries on by eye.
  • If you're a Lifeline contact, you don't need an app or an account. You get a message with a personal link to a plain page: I'm on my way, or I can't come.
  • Approvals, memory and the history of every task are there for you both to see.
  • The setup guide walks through installing AGENCY and giving it the permissions it needs.

Next: Download

Download

Get AGENCY OS for your Mac

Or try it in your browser first. Nothing to install.

Checking for the latest version…

Every version of AGENCY OS is on its releases page on GitHub.

Open the releases page on GitHub

What you need

  • macOS 13 Ventura or later
  • A Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) or an Intel processor
  • A webcam: the one built into a MacBook or iMac works
  • Google Chrome, for eye control on web pages (other apps work without it)
  • A Google Gemini API key for tasks the AI agent plans itself. Without one, AGENCY runs its built-in tasks only.
Which Mac do I have?
  1. Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of the screen, then About This Mac.
  2. If it lists a Chip such as Apple M1, M2, M3 or M4, you haveApple silicon.
  3. If it lists a Processor with “Intel” in its name, you have Intel.
  4. The same window shows your macOS version: it needs to be 13 (Ventura) or later.
If macOS says it can't open AGENCY

Until AGENCY OS is signed with an Apple Developer ID, macOS blocks it the first time. You only need to do this once per version.

  1. Open the downloaded .dmg and drag AGENCY into Applications.
  2. Open AGENCY from Applications. macOS says it can't verify it. Click Done (notMove to Bin).
  3. Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security. Scroll down toSecurity. Next to “AGENCY was blocked to protect your Mac”, clickOpen Anyway, and enter your Mac password or use Touch ID.
  4. Open AGENCY again and click Open Anyway once more.

On macOS 13 or 14 you can instead Control-click AGENCY in Applications, choose Open, thenOpen.

After each update of an unsigned build, macOS forgets that it allowed AGENCY to use Accessibility and Screen Recording. Turn them back on as in the setup guide. Signed builds don't have this problem.

To check the file is exactly the one we published, open Terminal and runshasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/ followed by the file's name. The result must match the SHA-256 shown above.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a special eye tracker?

No. AGENCY works with an ordinary webcam, like the one in a MacBook. Eye cursor works the moment the camera is on, with no setup. Eye gaze adds a 5-second eye scan: a light glides across the screen, then you look at three dots.

Webcam eye tracking is approximate, so AGENCY uses big, well-spaced buttons, a cursor that glides instead of jittering, and holds that survive a blink. Dedicated eye trackers aren't supported yet.

What if eye tracking doesn't work well for me?

AGENCY also works with a single switch (one button or a long blink, with choices highlighted in turn), with a head pointer, and with a mouse or keyboard for a helper.

Will it do things without asking me?

Not anything that matters. Paying, sending, signing, calling, deleting and sharing your details all need your approval of the exact action, and spending is capped at $50 a purchase and $100 a day by default. Stop halts everything at once, from any screen.

What happens when the internet is bad?

Every AI request goes through Synapse-Mesh, whose Cisco sentinel measures the network first. On a good network it runs Ultra-Fusion: Gemini with full thinking. When it's congested, Lean-Fusion: lighter thinking. When it's critical, Critical-Fusion: AGENCY's built-in plans, at once. Offline, Safe-Mode: built-in plans, and Lifeline retries its messages when the connection is back.

Does Lifeline call 911?

No. AGENCY never contacts emergency services by itself. Lifeline contacts the people you choose, and keeps contacting them until one of them says they're coming. They can call for an ambulance. Lifeline is not an emergency service and not a medical alarm, and it doesn't replace your ventilator's alarms.

Is my camera video uploaded anywhere?

No. Camera frames are processed on your computer and thrown away. They are never stored and never sent anywhere, including to the AI.

What does the AI see?

Only what a task you started needs: the text of your request and, when the agent has to look, the app it's working in. Screenshots aren't kept by default. Text on web pages, emails and documents is treated as information, never as instructions.

AI tasks need a Google Gemini API key, and Google's terms apply to what's sent. Without a key, AGENCY runs its built-in plans only.

Does it cost anything?

Downloading AGENCY OS from this page costs nothing, and there's nothing to buy here. If you use AI tasks, Google bills the account whose Gemini API key you use.

Is it a medical device?

No. AGENCY OS is not a medical device, a ventilator alarm or an emergency service, and it hasn't been clinically tested. It hasn't yet been evaluated with the people it's built for; that study is the next big piece of work.

Does it work on Windows, iPad or Linux?

Not yet. The Mac app relies on macOS accessibility features to work in every app. Tell us what you'd use, and we'll write back if that changes.
